title.narrative: Validation of Sustainable Land Management (SLM) models at the Landscape Scale

description.narrative: As explained in the CPP program document, this project, along with the other CPP projects, will have significant socio-economic benefits, enhancing food production and food security. It also ensures access to water supplies and reduces vulnerability to environmental disturbances. For the CPP as a whole, it is estimated that the production of staple crops will increase in the intervention areas by between 30 and 75% at the end of the Program implementation. Landscape-scale planning incorporates a new strategy that aims to ensure adapted land use planning that is consistent with physical, ecological, and social determinants. This strategy, once tested, will be applicable to the country as a whole, on different types of ecosystems. Increasing and improving the vegetation cover quality will also lead to a reduction in the population's vulnerability to environmental disturbances, such as hurricanes and droughts. These changes will be accompanied by increased employment opportunities (particularly for women), improvements in human and social capital (for example, strengthening individual capacity and awareness), better living conditions and reductions in rural migration to the city. The expected direct benefits of P4 project in the intervention areas: Restored area by SLM: 3,000 Ha Producers benefitted: 6,100 Direct beneficiaries: 9,600
Note: Disbursement data provided is cumulative and covers disbursement made by the project Agency.
Validate the Sustainable Land Management (SLM) models that have demonstrated effectiveness in the three previous CPP-OP15 projects at the landscape scale.
